target.title: feat(cli): improve editor handoffs for agents and humans
target.body:
## Summary

- add `crabbox open --json` with a versioned `crabbox/editor-handoff/v1` object for agents and other automation
- keep stdout machine-readable while workspace notices and diagnostics remain on stderr
- make the default terminal output easier to scan and copy with labeled SSH-command and remote-folder blocks
- state the foreground lease-activity, hard-TTL, Ctrl-C, and release behavior directly in the handoff
- document the child-process pattern for agents consuming the JSON handshake

## Why

https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/pull/1127 establishes the right generalized `open --editor=<name>` abstraction, but its only output is human prose and the command intentionally remains running. That makes agents scrape text and guess how to manage the foreground keepalive process, while humans have to select command and path values embedded inside numbered sentences.

This follow-up preserves the safety model from that PR: no background daemon, no SSH config or editor-setting mutation, no credential persistence, and no editor auto-launch.

## Agent UX

`--json` emits one newline-terminated object before waiting:

- editor identity
- lease id
- complete shell-quoted SSH command
- exact remote folder
- GitHub Actions hydration state
- foreground lease-activity and hard-TTL semantics
- release command when available

An agent can spawn Crabbox, decode the first object, use the handoff, and retain the child-process handle for the editor session.

## Human UX

The default output now provides:

- a clear ready state
- dedicated `SSH command` and `Remote folder` blocks
- short next steps
- explicit foreground activity and hard-TTL guidance
- a visible release command

## Validation

- `gofmt -w internal/cli/open.go internal/cli/open_test.go`
- added focused coverage for the human output and JSON contract
- full repository checks left to GitHub Actions because this execution environment could not clone GitHub or run the complete checkout

## Security and configuration

No secrets, configuration files, SSH config, or editor settings are written. Existing target restrictions and shell quoting are preserved.
